spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: S turns the phase of zeta on the critical line into the fluctuating remainder of the zero-counting formula, while S1 integrates that fluctuation into a smoother observable. The branch path and half-jump convention are doing real mathematical work: without them, the phase representation is not a well-defined zero-counting correction.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source defines S(t)=pi^(-1) Im log zeta(1/2+it), fixes continuous variation of log zeta along a specified path, assigns the midpoint value at jumps, and defines S1(t) as the integral of S from 0 to t. In the Riemann-von Mangoldt formula, S is the oscillatory correction to the smooth main term for N(t). Under RH, Theorem 2 gives a lower bound for max |S| on [T^beta,T] at the square-root scale sqrt(log T log log log T / log log T), and a positive lower bound for max S1 with an additional (log log T)^(-1) loss inside that scale.
directed.conceptual_reading: The zero set is represented indirectly by a smooth trend plus a phase fluctuation. Passing from S to S1 further compresses local jumps into accumulated deviation, trading localization for regularity and enabling a different kernel projection later.
